newsitem.title: USA: Schmalbach-Lubeca to buy Johnson PET unit for.
newsitem.headline: Schmalbach-Lubeca to buy Johnson PET unit for.

text.p: Johnson Controls Inc. said Monday it agreed to sell its plastic container division, the world's largest supplier of plastic beverage containers, to Schmalbach-Lubeca AG of Germany in a deal valued at about $645 million.

Terms of the transaction were not disclosed. But the 1 billion mark ($645 million) figure cited in German media reports was "not completely wrong," Schmalbach Finance Director Jan Maarten Henderson said in Duesseldorf, Germany, but declined to be more specific.
Milwaukee, Wis.-based Johnson Controls also makes automobile seats and other components and building control systems.

It said the sale would allow it to avoid issuing stock to help pay pay for the $1.4 billion acquisition of Prince Automotive, a maker of door panels, interior systems and other auto components, which was completed on Oct. 1.
Johnson said the operations being sold have annual sales of about $800 million. The transaction will not include its plastics machinery unit, Johnson said.
The deal requires approval by U.S. and European regulators and is expected to close in January, it said.

Schmalbach-Lubeca, a major German packaging producer, said the acquisition would make it a leading maker of PET plastic beverage and food bottles. PET stands for polyethylene terephthalate, a key plastics component.
